steps.content: Jane is sitting silently in the interrogation room, as if waiting for a judgment to be delivered on her.
You follow your question with a gesture that says, "Just play along and go through the motions."
Jane averts her gaze, seemingly unwilling to just go through the motions. You indicate the camera and let her know that you're being recorded.

steps.speaker: Player
steps.content: Practically speaking, he would be more useful alive than dead.

steps.speaker: Player
steps.content: We could've pried useful information on the criminal organization out of him...

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: He's more useful to me dead.
Jane interrupts you and takes over the conversation. Shaking your head, you decide to indulge her.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: The year the life of my family was turned upside down, my father was still a sheriff.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: He was a kind and upstanding man. He wouldn't tolerate any injustice. This got him into a lot of trouble.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: I admired him greatly. I thought he was the perfect example of a good sheriff. I wanted to become a virtuous sheriff just like him.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Tragedy struck when he was investigating a case involving Nirvana. Nirvana didn't like the idea of someone looking into their business.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Mysteriously and suddenly, he was heavily in debt to some loan shark. They broke his arms and legs and locked him up.
Jane gives a bitter laugh and continues.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Since my father couldn't pay off the debts, they came after my mother and me. We sold everything valuable in our house, but it wasn't enough. I tried many ways to make money, but it was just a drop in the bucket.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Those debt collectors threatened us on a daily basis. One day, they tried to kidnap my mom and sell her for money.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: I remember that day clearly. It was the first time I'd ever shot someone. Fifteen bullets in the magazine, one for each debt collector. They lay flat on the floor, every one of them.

steps.speaker: Player
steps.content: That was when you became a Sinner?

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Yes. I had to protect my mom. I awakened my power as I was shooting the debt collectors.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: But... it was not a good thing, having this new power. Because of it, I was in constant danger of losing my self-control, and I became hypersensitive to blood, bullets, and crime.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Every day, I tried my best to control my emotions and mental state, even while I was in the <color=#fb9259>Ghosts</color>.

options: When did you and Coleman first meet?

choices.text: When did you and Coleman first meet?

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Right after I took down those debt collectors.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: He said he liked my new power, and that we were birds of a feather. He took care of those debt collectors, and covered the whole thing up so no one knew their whereabouts.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: He said he would keep my parents safe if I joined the <color=#fb9259>Ghosts</color> and worked for him, which involved robbing banks all around Eastside.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: In fact, he did. Sadly, that also afforded him the leverage to control me.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: The new power was constantly corrupting me. Every time I stormed into a bank, I heard a voice in my head, my own voice.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: It told me to kill everyone in the bank and leave with the money.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: When I put the money in front of Coleman, the voice would say, "You should've kept some. No one would've known."

options: Did you listen to that voice?

choices.text: Did you listen to that voice?

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: No. Never.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: I wanted out after a few bank jobs. I wanted to stay by my parents' side. Money would be tight, I knew, but I could find normal work and support them with the salary.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: But it was easy to get in, impossible to get out. Coleman would never allow it. Once you joined the <color=#fb9259>Ghosts</color>, he practically owned you.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: He would never let me go. Each of my solo bank jobs brought him millions, tens of millions, of DisCoins. He was hell-bent on turning me into <color=#fb9259>Coleman</color> 2.0.

steps.speaker: Option
options: He was grooming you to become his successor?

choices.text: He was grooming you to become his successor?

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Yes, otherwise... he would've killed me long ago.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: I had so many weaknesses. It would've been so easy for him to kill me. He kept me alive, because I was still useful to him.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: So I worked for him for another year, as a bank robber.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Before entering a bank, I would repeatedly tell myself, "Don't kill. Don't hurt anyone. Just take the money and leave." To keep my mind from being completely overtaken by my corrupting power, I strove to finish a bank job within two minutes.
Jane sighs and shakes her head.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Those days were a living hell. On one hand, I was forced to rob banks. On the other, I was scared that my parents might get hurt again.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Day in day out... I was on the brink of losing my sanity.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Roughly a year ago, when I was desperate for a break, I told him I needed some time away from him and the organization, and that I wouldn't reveal anything about the Ghosts to anyone.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: He did. In his eyes, I was just one of his puppets.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: He didn't stop me even when I joined the Public Security Bureau. Because he knew he had a myriad of ways to bring me back to the fold.

steps.speaker: Option
options: How did you manage to get into the Public Security Bureau?

choices.text: How did you manage to get into the Public Security Bureau?

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Well... I passed the exam. It wasn't hard.
Jane blinks, as if it's the most ordinary thing.

steps.speaker: Player
steps.content: They must have done a background check on you. They didn't find out you were a bank robber?

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: I'd never been caught, nor had anyone ever discovered my identity. So in official records, I was still "daughter of a former sheriff."

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: After I joined the Public Security Bureau, for a year, I lived a much simpler life. I carried out my duties as a new sheriff, I did what I was familiar with. And I... did good deeds.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: I wanted to do as many good deeds as possible, catch as many bad guys as possible. I wanted to repay the 37 million DisCoins I'd stolen.
She takes out the note she received from Coleman in the hospital and tears it to shreds.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: I thought I could leave my past behind, but I was wrong. No matter how many good deeds I did, I would always be a robber. The crimes I committed followed me anywhere I went.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: As long as I was alive, I would always be a bank robber.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: As long as Coleman was alive, as long as this madman was still breathing, my nightmare would never end.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: I decided to seek mutual destruction. If I was dead, my debt of 37 million DisCoins would go away, in a way; if he was dead, no one would ever know my past.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: So with your help, I did what I hadn't had the courage to do on the fateful day by shooting him in the head...

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Using the bullet I had kept with me since that day to pierce a head harder than Hypercube.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Unfortunately, killing the madman didn't bring back what I'd lost. I can never get my old life back.

steps.speaker: Option
options: You might still have a chance.

choices.text: You might still have a chance.

steps.content: You lift the restraint the shackles are exerting on Jane and place a document in front of her.

In stopping the robbery of the Bank of Eastside, Trainee Sheriff Jane carried out her duties outstandingly and fearlessly. She annihilated the <color=#fb9259>Ghosts</color>, an organization of bank robbers long active in Eastside, and prevented significant economic losses the region might have suffered if not for her valiant actions.
Such actions would merit the granting of the Eastside Sheriff Medal of Excellence under normal circumstances. However, given Sheriff Jane's special identity and alleged association with the <color=#fb9259>Ghosts</color>, and after considering her contributions and mistakes, the Eastside Public Security Bureau has decided not to reward or punish her.
She shall continue her service to the Eastside Public Security as a sheriff, if she so chooses.

steps.speaker: Player
steps.content: This is Eastside's decision.

steps.speaker: Player
steps.content: You have a decision to make yourself. You can go back to Eastside, or you can go home and be with your parents.

steps.speaker: Player
steps.content: You're free to make your own choices now. This is great news for you.
You extend your hand to Jane, who is free to go now. She takes your hand. You try to pull her up.
But she shows no intention of getting up, holding your hand firmly.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: You mean...

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: I, a former member of the <color=#fb9259>Ghosts</color>, am being released without charge?

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Just because I killed Coleman?

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: I would have nothing against such an arrangement, if I had died in the bank.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Yes, I did.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: And I will spend the rest of my new life repenting my sins.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: I'll repay the 37 million DisCoins I stole, and rectify the damage caused by my collusion with the <color=#fb9259>Ghosts</color> and my inaction as a member of the Public Security Bureau.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: If I walked out of this interrogation room today without having to suffer the consequences of my past actions, Eastside would likely be plagued with more criminal organizations like the <color=#fb9259>Ghosts</color>, more madmen like Coleman.
Upon seeing how determined Jane is, you decide not to dissuade her.

steps.speaker: Player
steps.content: Eastside has decided not to punish you, but the MBCC still can. I have a proposal here that I'd like you to relay to your sheriff friend.
You clear your throat and present your proposal.

steps.speaker: Player
steps.content: She will become a Sinner under the authority of the MBCC from now on. Does she agree?

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: She agrees.

steps.speaker: Player
steps.content: She will follow orders willingly and participate in fights against Corruptors. Does she agree?

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: She agrees.

steps.speaker: Player
steps.content: All her income will automatically go to the Bank of Eastside until she's paid the full amount of money due. Does she agree?

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: She agrees.

steps.speaker: Player
steps.content: By becoming an MBCC Sinner, she will be forever seen as an outcast in the public eye and will have to endure slanders. Does she accept this?

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: She does.

steps.speaker: Player
steps.content: By becoming an MBCC Sinner, she will forever be restrained by the shackles. Does she accept this?

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: She does.
However, if she proves herself capable of keeping her power under control and giving up robbing banks, then I will...
You trail off deliberately.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Then you will what?
Then I will give her considerable freedom. She'll be able to visit her parents whom she hasn't seen for a long time and take some time off to care for them.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Deal.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: I'm sure she will be very happy to hear this.

steps.speaker: Logistics Worker A
steps.content: The new girl with the helmet, she's a true workaholic.

steps.speaker: Logistics Worker B
steps.content: How so?

steps.speaker: Logistics Worker A
steps.content: She moved that mountain of stuff in the Supply Office into position in two hours.

steps.speaker: Logistics Worker B
steps.content: Really? Those things must have weighed at least a few tons. Is she even human?

steps.speaker: Logistics Worker A
steps.content: Maybe she's not.

steps.speaker: Logistics Worker B
steps.content: What?

steps.speaker: Logistics Worker A
steps.content: I mean, she may be a Sinner, I think.

steps.speaker: Logistics Worker B
steps.content: A Sinner working in the logistics department? Now Sinners are competing with us for low-paying jobs?

steps.speaker: Logistics Worker A
steps.content: Not just logistics. I hear she can do a lot of other things, like paperwork and firearm maintenance.

steps.speaker: Logistics Worker A
steps.content: What's more ridiculous is she also participates in field missions!

steps.speaker: Logistics Worker B
steps.content: Really? She sounds like a real busy bee. I wonder why the bureau hired me.

steps.speaker: Logistics Worker A
steps.content: Well, some people around here are lazy. That fella with the eyepatch in the depot is one example. He's always slacking. Some are even worse, sleeping in broad daylight, and on their feet. Now with this new girl, things kind of balance out.

steps.speaker: Logistics Worker B
steps.content: You have a point...
You stand at the corner where two passageways meet, listening in on the conversation between the two logistics workers.
Ever since Jane, a Sinner who doubles as a logistics worker, joined the bureau, everyone has become much more active.
Despite looking cold and distant on the outside, she is actually very approachable.
You stretch. You're heading to your office to start work when your communication device beeps. It's a message from Jane.
